tables.heading: Read replicas, Multi-AZ deployments, and multi-region deployments
tables.header_text: | Multi-AZ deployments | Multi-Region deployments | Read replicas |

rows.text: | Main purpose is high availability | Main purpose is disaster recovery and local performance | Main purpose is scalability |

cells.Multi-Region deployments: Main purpose is disaster recovery and local performance

rows.text: | Non-Aurora: synchronous replication; Aurora: synchronous replication | Asynchronous replication | Asynchronous replication |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Non-Aurora: synchronous replication; Aurora: synchronous replication

rows.text: | Non-Aurora: only the primary instance is active; Aurora: all instances are active | All regions are accessible and can be used for reads | All read replicas are accessible and can be used for read scaling |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Non-Aurora: only the primary instance is active; Aurora: all instances are active
cells.Multi-Region deployments: All regions are accessible and can be used for reads
cells.Read replicas: All read replicas are accessible and can be used for read scaling

rows.text: | Non-Aurora: automated backups are taken from standby; Aurora: automated backups are taken from shared storage layer | Automated backups can be taken in each region | No backups configured by default |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Non-Aurora: automated backups are taken from standby; Aurora: automated backups are taken from shared storage layer
cells.Multi-Region deployments: Automated backups can be taken in each region

rows.text: | Always span at least two Availability Zones within a single region | Each region can have a Multi-AZ deployment | Can be within an Availability Zone, Cross-AZ, or Cross-Region |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Always span at least two Availability Zones within a single region
cells.Multi-Region deployments: Each region can have a Multi-AZ deployment
cells.Read replicas: Can be within an Availability Zone, Cross-AZ, or Cross-Region

rows.text: | Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrades happen on primary; Aurora: all instances are updated together | Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrade is independent in each region; Aurora: all instances are updated together | Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrade is independent from source instance; Aurora: all instances are updated together |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrades happen on primary; Aurora: all instances are updated together
cells.Multi-Region deployments: Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrade is independent in each region; Aurora: all instances are updated together
cells.Read replicas: Non-Aurora: database engine version upgrade is independent from source instance; Aurora: all instances are updated together

rows.text: | Automatic failover to standby (non-Aurora) or read replica (Aurora) when a problem is detected | Aurora allows promotion of a secondary region to be the primary | Can be manually promoted to a standalone database instance (non-Aurora) or to be the primary instance (Aurora) |

cells.Multi-AZ deployments: Automatic failover to standby (non-Aurora) or read replica (Aurora) when a problem is detected
cells.Multi-Region deployments: Aurora allows promotion of a secondary region to be the primary
cells.Read replicas: Can be manually promoted to a standalone database instance (non-Aurora) or to be the primary instance (Aurora)
